title: Conflict-Averse Gradient Descent for Multi-Task Learning
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
problem_statement: Optimizing the average loss across multiple tasks with shared parameters suffers from conflicting gradients where task gradients differ in magnitude and direction, causing the average gradient update to harm specific tasks and causing prior gradient manipulation methods (MGDA, PCGrad) to converge to arbitrary Pareto-stationary points without guarantees of minimizing the average loss.
domain: Multi-Task Learning — multi-task supervised vision (NYU-v2, CityScapes, Multi-Fashion+MNIST), multi-task reinforcement learning (Meta-World MT10/MT50), and semi-supervised learning with auxiliary tasks (CIFAR-10)
theoretical_framework: Multi-objective optimization and Pareto optimality, where CAGrad maximizes the worst local improvement min_i <g_i, d> within a trust ball around the average gradient g0, with hyperparameter c controlling convergence to the average loss optimum (c<1) versus Pareto set (c≥1), including GD (c=0) and MGDA (c→∞) as special cases.
methodology: Conflict-Averse Gradient Descent (CAGrad) solves max_d min_i <g_i, d> subject to ||d - g0|| ≤ c||g0||, where g0 is the average gradient and c∈[0,1) ensures convergence to a stationary point of the average loss L0. The high-dimensional primal is converted to a low-dimensional dual min_{w∈W} g_w^T g0 + c||g0||·||g_w|| over simplex W={w≥0, sum w=1} with g_w=Σ w_i g_i, solved via standard convex solvers, yielding update d*= g0 + c||g0||/||g_w*|| · g_w*. A practical speedup samples subset S⊂[K] and retains convergence. All experiments build on MTAN (SegNet) for vision and Soft Actor-Critic for RL.
datasets: Synthetic 2D two-task toy optimization with 5 initial points to visualize conflicting gradients and Pareto set
Multi-Fashion+MNIST — 120k FashionMNIST+MNIST overlaid images for two-task classification, trained with shrunken LeNet (Adam 1e-3, 50 epochs, batch 256)
NYU-v2 — 13-class segmentation, depth, and surface normals (795 train / 654 test) on MTAN-SegNet backbone under equal weighting
CityScapes — 7-class segmentation and depth on MTAN-SegNet under equal weighting
Meta-World MT10 and MT50 — 10 and 50 robotic manipulation tasks evaluated with Soft Actor-Critic, success rate averaged over 10 runs
CIFAR-10 semi-supervised — 50k training images with 500/1000/2000 labeled, 10% validation, using ARML and GradNorm loss formulations with two auxiliary unsupervised losses and Adam 200 epochs

metrics: Toy: optimization trajectories and final training losses per task and average loss
Multi-Fashion+MNIST: average and per-task training losses over 3 runs

NYU-v2/CityScapes: mIoU and Pixel Accuracy for segmentation, Abs/Rel Error for depth, Mean/Median angle distance and within 11.25°/22.5°/30° for normals, and average per-task performance drop Δm % versus single-task SegNet, with two-tailed Student t-test (p=0.1)
Meta-World: mean success rate ± stderr over 10 runs, and training time per epoch
CIFAR-10 semi-supervised: average test accuracy ± std over 3 runs for ARML+methods and GradNorm+methods
baselines: Vanilla gradient descent (GD / Adam) on average loss
Multiple Gradient Descent Algorithm (MGDA, Sener & Koltun)
Projecting Conflicting Gradients (PCGrad, Yu et al.)
Cross-Stitch Networks and MTAN for architecture baselines
GradDrop, IMTL-G, RotoGrad (referenced), Multi-task SAC variants, Task Encoder, Soft Modularization, CARE
ARML baseline and GradNorm baseline for semi-supervised learning, each combined with PCGrad/MGDA/CAGrad
architectures: MTAN on SegNet (VGG-based encoder-decoder) for NYU-v2 and CityScapes
Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) multi-layer perceptron actor-critic for Meta-World
WRN-28-10 style backbone for CIFAR-10 ARML (as in ARML original)

key_findings: CAGrad balances tasks while provably converging to the average loss optimum when 0≤c<1 (Theorem 3.2: sum ||∇L0||² bounded by 2(L0(θ0)-L0*)/α(1-c²)), whereas c≥1 converges to arbitrary Pareto-stationary points; c=0 recovers GD and c→∞ recovers MGDA, verified on toy example with 5 initializations where GD stuck in 2/5 runs and MGDA/PCGrad scattered across Pareto set while CAGrad converged to average optimum.

On NYU-v2, CAGrad (c=0.4 on MTAN) achieves 39.79 mIoU, 65.49 Pix Acc, 0.5486 Abs Err, 26.31 Mean angle and Δm=0.20%, outperforming MTAN (5.59%), PCGrad (3.97%), GradDrop (3.58%), Cross-Stitch (6.96%) and significantly improving the overlooked surface normal task while matching others.
On CityScapes, CAGrad (c=0.2) achieves 75.16 mIoU and 0.0141 Abs Err with Δm=11.64%, halving MTAN’s drop (22.60%) and outperforming PCGrad (18.29%) and improving depth over other methods.

On Meta-World, CAGrad attains 0.83±0.045 on MT10 and 0.52±0.023 on MT50, surpassing Multi-task SAC (0.49/0.36), PCGrad (0.72/0.50) and Soft Modularization (0.73/0.50), trailing only CARE (0.84/0.54) which uses extra language metadata; CAGrad-Fast sampling 4/8 tasks retains 0.82/0.50 while giving 2× and 5× speedup over PCGrad.

In semi-supervised CIFAR-10, ARML+CAGrad reaches 68.25% (500 labels), 74.37% (1000), 82.81% (2000) versus ARML 67.05/73.22/81.35 and ARML+PCGrad 67.49/73.23/81.91; MGDA collapses (49.27% at 500 labels) by over-optimizing auxiliary tasks away from main loss, confirming CAGrad’s average-loss guarantee matters when main plus auxiliary objectives are not symmetric.
Efficiency overhead is modest: dual optimization over K≤50 weights is far cheaper than K backpropagations, and subset sampling maintains performance with O(|S|N+T) cost.
scope_and_delimitations: Evaluated with fixed backbones per domain (shrunken LeNet, MTAN-SegNet, SAC) under equal loss weighting for vision and not with exhaustive architecture search or uncertainty weighting.
Tuned c only in {0.1…0.9} (best 0.2–0.4 for vision, implicit for RL) and reported means over 3 seeds (vision) or 10 runs (RL) without testing c adaptively per task or per layer.

Compared gradient manipulation at the shared parameter level and not layer-wise or task-specific head gradients, and assumed average loss as main objective L0 without exploring other user-specified main objectives mentioned as future direction.
Semi-supervised experiments held out fixed 10% validation and used the same labeled subsets for all methods, not testing varied label proportions beyond 500/1000/2000 or non-CIFAR datasets.

limitations.verbatim_excerpt: While we focus mainly on optimizing the average loss, an interesting future direction is to look at main objectives other than the average loss under the multi-task setting.
limitations.summary: Authors acknowledge CAGrad focuses on the average loss as main objective and has not been validated for other main objectives; implicit limitations include need to tune c per dataset, extra convex optimization per step (though small), and evaluation limited to up to 50 tasks.

generalizability_gap: CAGrad was not evaluated on large-scale language or code-switched NLP tasks, on transformer-based language models, or on multi-modal vision-language settings; nor on highly unbalanced task counts (hundreds) or explicit noisy low-resource code-switching relevant to this repository’s broader MTL survey.
methodological_gap: CAGrad computes gradients at full shared parameters and does not model layer-wise conflict, task grouping, or Pareto front coverage; it requires solving a simplex optimization each step and inherits dependence on accurate stochastic gradients, without comparison to second-order or curvature-aware balancing.
future_work: Extending CAGrad to main objectives other than the average loss and to alternative MTL architectures beyond shared-backbone models.
Adaptive per-layer or per-step selection of c and integration with language or code-switched NLP benchmarks.
Exploring combination with task grouping or routing networks for scaling to hundreds of tasks.
